commenti.body:
Oh “8th Grade” is this for me. I haven’t seen it in a while but it felt soooo real in its depiction of that awkward part of life with the added anxiety? of wanting to be noticed/seen in a very digital world in which everyone else seem to be doing the same. 

I also heard great things about “Petite Maman”!

John and Faith Hubley were kicked out of traditional Hollywood for refusing to denounce communism during the red scare, purely on freedom of speech grounds. They began recording their children's conversations and animating them. They are unique looks into the free form flow of a child's mind. The Hubleys would be nominated for 7 academy awards and win 3.

This is my favorite example.

https://youtu.be/4O8VE4qB8-s?feature=shared

Just off the top of my head with interesting children scenes would include *Children of Heaven* 1997, *Pather Panchali*, and maybe some of the old Tom Sawyer/Huck Finn films.

"Fish Tank" by Andrea Arnold is a good pick for this. The protagonist Mia, is shown to the audience as  hardened and detached to the circumstances that she grows up in, but as the film progresses, they are made aware just how naive and idealistic she is. Just a heartbreaking depiction of adolescent girlhood, not an easy watch but a fantastic film, nonetheless.

Addie Pray from Peter Bogdanovich's "Paper Moon" may not be as much of a good fit, but Tatum O'Neal performance is really multifaceted. As sharp and perceptive as an adult, yet retaining the innocence and open-heartedness of a child, she's a good example of children being seen and portrayed as complex individuals.

Hope it helps.

PETITE MAMAN (2021, Celine Sciamma) is a perfect film like this from one of the best directors working today.  Her other films, WATER LILIES and GIRLHOOD are also very good.  Older stuff like THE RED BALOON or WHITE MANE.  Iranian movies are kind of their own thing, and women have a whole other level of challenges there, but there were a string of kid based movies in the late 90s/early 2000s like THE WHITE BALOON, CHILDREN OF HEAVEN, etc.

My Neighbor Totoro. I was struck by how authentic the children felt. All hyperness and imagination and emotional reaction! Tons of scenes of the sisters playing with each other, their dad, the forest spirits.

The overall plot is about them coping with their mom being in the hospital. Little sister is more naive, thinking some fresh-grown corn will be enough to cure her mom. The drama culminates in the older sister responding to her toddler sister's complaints with, "Do you want mom to die!?" making her cry and run away. But the movie is very much at the comprehension level of a small child.

The scene in Welcome to the Dollhouse where Dawn (Heather Matarazzo) and her classmate/bully, both age 12-13, matter-of-factly discuss getting “finger-fucked” by the 18 year old neighborhood creep, ‘Steve’. Dawn’s classmate tells her, with the gravity of a doctor breaking terrible news, that she is too ugly for ‘Steve’ to want to violate.

Include the scene afterwards, where Dawn flirts with Steve (played by a full-on adult man, jarring next to the 12 year old actresses) and it becomes clear that she doesn’t know what Steve actually did to her classmate. She just waves her hands around and says “look at my fingers,” it’s played for laughs, but the audience knows that the adult onscreen had digitally raped another very young child, one who lacked the vocabulary to express what he’d actually done. Usually, movies that glorify such relationships (original script of Raiders, for example, or The Professional) don’t feature the child speaking with peers about their experience, putting what they went through in their own limited words.
Ooh thank you I will look into these!
